title: Proctor Landing Park
subtitle: Bridging Community & Ecology to Support Public Health
collaborators: Academic capstone; no client or firm of record
summary: A flood-prone civic landscape on the Ohio River, near Paddy and Symmes Creeks, redesigned to preserve and improve ecological function while providing flood-resilient recreation that measurably supports public health. The attitude throughout: design with water, not against it.

sections.heading: Brief
sections.body: How can a flood-prone civic landscape keep its ecological function and still give a community diverse, durable recreation? The design integrates circulation, hydrology, habitat, recreation, and community use into a single public framework organized around a Paddy Creek ecological core.

sections.heading: Site analysis
sections.body: Floodplain, hydrology, soils, topography, and circulation analysis built on FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer data, USDA NRCS and Ohio soils, Region 7 watershed planning, Census demographics, and public-health research. The evidence set the program: flood-prone land becomes working landscape, not fenced-off risk.

sections.heading: Design
sections.body: Wetland creation, riparian restoration, and flood-adaptive planting anchor the ecological core. A connected exercise loop links boardwalk sequences, timber bridges, overlooks, and contemplative paths with active recreation: sports fields and courts, play areas, a splash pad, a dog park, and a multimodal bus-and-bike arrival. Recreation coexists with periodic flooding rather than pretending the floodplain is dry upland.

sections.heading: Production
sections.body: Master plan, CAD plans, sections, two axonometric views, system diagrams, planting matrices for woodland, upland, wetland, and riparian zones, bridge and culvert design development, phasing, takeoffs, and a stewardship framework.

sections.heading: Recognition
sections.body: DAAPWorks 2026 Director's Choice Gallery. SEGD Experiential Design Honorable Mention. Selected for Design Museum of Chicago DAAPworks exhibition.
